cleanIntro: The S20 Hunter is a modular bolt rifle: the barrelled receiver, the buttstock and the fore-end all come off a STOCK BASE, and Sako gives torque figures for putting them back. ⛔ Read one sentence before anything else — Sako says corrosion can begin WITHIN 24 HOURS if the rifle is not cleaned after use, and that this holds for the All-weather and Stainless models too. ⚠ Two smaller things bite: the firing pin can only be decocked with the bolt CLOSED, and the bolt-stop pin is spring-preloaded and will leave the receiver if you are careless with it.

steps.title: ⛔ RED DOT SHOWING means the safety is OFF
steps.action: Read the safety before you touch anything else. On this rifle the RED DOT visible means the SAFETY IS DISENGAGED and the rifle is ready to fire; when the red dot is not visible the safety is ENGAGED. It is the opposite of the convention some shooters carry from other rifles.
steps.prose: Red showing is danger, not readiness confirmed. Learn it on this rifle before you learn it the other way.
steps.quote: When the safety button shows the red dot, the SAFETY IS DISENGAGED and the rifle is ready to fire. When the red dot is not visible, the SAFETY IS ENGAGED.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Safety, p.10

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt out, chamber checked — and the S20 magazine does not lift
steps.action: Depress the front part of the magazine inward while pushing the release button backwards. ⚠ On the S20 the magazine does NOT have to be lifted before opening the magazine release — that differs from other rifles in this same book. Then remove the bolt: lift the bolt handle, press the bolt stop button and pull the bolt completely out. Then look in the chamber.
steps.prose: A one-line difference between models in a four-model book, and it is the one that makes an S20 magazine feel stuck to someone used to a Sako 90.
steps.quote: • Remove the bolt by lifting the bolt handle, pressing the bolt stop button and completely pulling the bolt out of the receiver.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Load Check, p.10

steps.title: ⚠ The firing pin decocks only with the bolt CLOSED
steps.action: To decock: attach the bolt to the receiver, close it, point the rifle in a safe direction and pull the trigger. Sako states plainly that the firing pin can be decocked ONLY when the bolt is in the closed position — trying it with the bolt out achieves nothing.
steps.prose: Storing a bolt rifle with the firing pin cocked is what sets a spring over years. This is the two-second habit that avoids it.
steps.quote: The firing pin can be decocked only when the bolt is in the closed position.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Load Check — Notice, p.10

steps.title: ⛔ OBSTRUCTION CHECK — look through the bore before every session
steps.action: With the rifle confirmed unloaded, check the barrel for obstructions in the chamber and bore. Sako calls this extremely important and says why: serious injury can result if a cartridge is fired in an obstructed barrel or chamber.
steps.prose: This is a separate named check in Sako's book, not a footnote to cleaning. It comes before shooting, not after cleaning.
steps.quote: Check the barrel to ensure there are no obstructions in the chamber and bore.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Obstruction Check, p.10

steps.title: Buttstock off — two fastening screws, and 7 Nm going back
steps.action: With the rifle unloaded and the bolt and magazine out, loosen the two fastening screws and pull the buttstock out. ⚠ Note the reassembly figure now, because it is in the same step: those two screws go back to 7 Nm.
steps.prose: A torque figure on a stock screw is Sako telling you the bedding matters. Guessing it is how a rifle loses its zero between cleanings.
steps.quote: Remove the buttstock as follows (fig. 29): 1. Make sure that the rifle is not loaded with ammunition. 2. Remove the bolt and the magazine. 3. Loosen the two fastening screws (A, fig. 29). 4. Pull out the buttstock (B, fig. 29). 5. When you reassemble, tighten the two fastening screws to 7 Nm (A, fig. 29).
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Buttstock (Sako S20), p.14

steps.title: ⚠ HUNTER-ONLY — the fore-end comes off the SLING SWIVEL STUD
steps.action: This is the step that is yours and not the Precision's. On the S20 HUNTER the fore-end is released by removing the SLING SWIVEL STUD WITH A WASHER; on the S20 Precision it is two M-LOK fastening screws instead. Take the right one off and pull the fore-end out of the stock base.
steps.prose: Two rifles, one page, two different fasteners. Looking for M-LOK screws on a Hunter is looking for something that is not there.
steps.quote: 4. Sako S20 Hunter: Remove the sling swivel stud with a washer, two
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Barreled Receiver (Sako S20), step 4, p.14

steps.title: Barrelled receiver out of the stock base — and mind the magazine spring
steps.action: With the buttstock and fore-end off, remove the two fastening screws with their washers, the magazine guide and the SPRING, then lift the barrelled receiver out of the stock base. ⚠ The spring is a loose part in that sequence — keep it with the guide.
steps.prose: This is a modular chassis pretending to be a stock. Everything is a fastener and a washer, and everything goes back the same way.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the two fastening screws with washers, magazine guide and spring (G, fig. 29). And remove the barreled
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Barreled Receiver (Sako S20), step 6, p.14

steps.title: ⛔ CORROSION CAN BEGIN WITHIN 24 HOURS — even on stainless
steps.action: Clean the rifle right after use, EVEN IF YOU DID NOT SHOOT. Sako is explicit that maintenance must not be neglected on the "All-weather" or "Stainless" models either, and that corrosion can begin within 24 hours if the rifle is not cleaned after use.
steps.prose: "Even without shooting" is the clause that catches people — a day in the rain counts as use.
steps.quote: Routine cleaning should always take place right after use of the rifle (even without shooting). Maintenance should not be neglected even in case of the “All-weather” or “Stainless” models. Corrosion can begin within 24 hours if the rifle is not cleaned after use.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Routine Cleaning, p.20

steps.title: Bronze brush 10-15 push-pulls — and use a ROD GUIDE
steps.action: Use an absolutely straight, sturdy and smooth cleaning rod with a BRONZE bore brush soaked in bore solvent, and push-pull it through until the major residue is gone — Sako's figure is roughly 10 to 15 times. ⚠ Use a cleaning rod GUIDE: it stops the rod dragging on the inner surfaces of the bore.
steps.prose: On a rifle bought for accuracy the rod is the thing most likely to damage it. The guide is not an accessory here, it is part of the instruction.
steps.quote: 3. Use an absolutely straight, sturdy and smooth cleaning rod fitted with bronze bore brush soaked in bore solvent and push-pull it through the bore until major residue is removed (approx. 10-15 times).
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Routine Cleaning, step 3, p.20

steps.title: ⛔ Felt pellets — ONE DIRECTION ONLY, fresh one every pass
steps.action: Push a clean felt pellet moistened with solvent through the bore, one after another, until they come out clean — roughly 5 to 10. ⛔ Clean ONLY in the direction of bullet movement, and replace the dirty pellet with a new one BEFORE every sequence. Guide the rod with your fingers or a bore guide.
steps.prose: Dragging a dirty pellet back through is re-laying the fouling you just removed, which is why Sako makes the replacement part of the step.
steps.quote: 4. Push a clean felt pellet moistened with cleaning solvent through the bore one after another until pellets come out clean (approx. 5-10 times). Clean only in the direction of bullet movement and replace dirty pellet with new before every cleaning sequence.
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Routine Cleaning, step 4, p.20

steps.title: Both stock screws back to 7 Nm
steps.action: Fore-end into the stock base and its fastener refitted — sling swivel stud and washer on a Hunter. Barrelled receiver into the stock base with its two screws, washers, magazine guide and spring. Buttstock on, and the two fastening screws tightened to 7 Nm.
steps.prose: One torque figure, used twice. Write it on the inside of the case lid.
steps.quote: 7. When you reassemble, tighten the two fastening screws to 7 Nm (A, fig. 29).
steps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Barreled Receiver (Sako S20), step 7, p.14

deepSteps.title: ⚠ The bolt-stop pin is SPRING-PRELOADED and can leave the receiver
deepSteps.action: The pin in the bolt stop is preloaded by its spring. Sako's warning is that it may come OUT of the receiver if the components are handled carelessly — so work over a tray whenever the bolt stop is being pressed or the bolt is coming in and out repeatedly.
deepSteps.prose: A small sprung pin that leaves a receiver on a carpet is a rifle out of action for a week.
deepSteps.quote: The pin in the bolt stop is preloaded by the spring. However, it may come out of the receiver, if the components are handled carelessly.
deepSteps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Bolt Stop, p.14

deepSteps.title: Periodic maintenance — at least once a year, and copper is what you are chasing
deepSteps.action: Beyond the after-every-use routine, Sako asks for periodic maintenance at least once a year, and more often under heavy use or severe conditions. That is the pass where copper from the bullet jacket comes out, with a solvent or mechanical cleaner made for it.
deepSteps.prose: Two schedules, and they do different jobs: the daily one stops corrosion, the annual one restores the bore.
deepSteps.quote: Periodic maintenance should be carried out at least once a year or more frequently under heavy use or in severe conditions.
deepSteps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Periodic Maintenance, p.21

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Nothing older than TEN YEARS goes down this barrel
deepSteps.action: Sako sets an age limit on ammunition: do not fire ammunition over 10 years old in this firearm. Primers, powder, cases and bullets deteriorate, and the result can damage the rifle or injure the shooter. Inspect every cartridge for splits, deformation and dents before it goes in the magazine — factory ammunition included.
deepSteps.prose: An explicit shelf life is rare in a manual. It is here because a hangfire in a bolt rifle is a face-height event.
deepSteps.quote: Do not fire old (age over 10 years) ammunition in this firearm.
deepSteps.cite: SAKO 90 / S20 / QUAD / FINNFIRE II OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Ammunition, p.10

cleaning.name: AFTER EVERY USE — EVEN WITHOUT SHOOTING
tasks: ⛔ Corrosion can begin within 24 hours — stainless and All-weather included
Rifle confirmed unloaded and the firing pin confirmed decocked
Bronze bore brush in solvent, push-pull approx. 10-15 times
⚠ Cleaning rod GUIDE used — it keeps the rod off the bore's inner surfaces
Felt pellets until they come out clean, approx. 5-10
⛔ One direction only — the direction of bullet movement

cleaning.name: PERIODIC — AT LEAST ANNUALLY
tasks: More often under heavy use or in severe conditions
Copper fouling from the bullet jacket addressed with a solvent or mechanical cleaner

cleaning.name: STOCK AND FASTENERS
tasks: Two buttstock fastening screws — 7 Nm on reassembly
Hunter fore-end: sling swivel stud with a washer
Magazine guide and its SPRING kept together
⚠ Bolt-stop pin is spring-preloaded — work over a tray

reassembly: Barrelled receiver into the stock base; two screws with washers, magazine guide and spring.
Fore-end into the stock base; sling swivel stud and washer refitted (Hunter).
Buttstock on; two fastening screws to 7 Nm.
Bolt in, closed, and the firing pin decocked with the muzzle safe.
Magazine seated; bore confirmed clear before any live round.
fncheck: ⛔ Obstruction check first — look through the chamber and bore and confirm nothing is in either; Sako makes this its own named check because a cartridge fired in an obstructed barrel injures people. Then: bolt in and cycling freely, bolt stop retaining it, magazine seating and releasing (remember the S20's magazine does not lift before the release opens). Work the safety and confirm the RED DOT SHOWING means FIRE. Close the bolt and decock the firing pin with the muzzle safe — it will not decock with the bolt open. Confirm both stock screws are at 7 Nm.
